clue.text: A temperature examined and reported in trial

parts.note: taken as written
T is the standard abbreviation for temperature
to examine something is to test it

explanation.surface: A patient's temperature was taken, and the reading was reported as evidence in a clinical trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trial' suggests a medical study, but the definition means a courtroom trial where witnesses give evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness formally, so something attested was declared on oath, as testimony is in court.

clue.text: Property stupid people distributed over time

indicators.note: things distributed are spread around and so end up in a new order

parts.note: asses are fools
T is the usual abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Foolish heirs have scattered the family's property over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: The fools and the time letter are mixed together as one batch.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are the things of value a person or company owns, which is what property means here.

clue.text: Notes we hear from singers in famous trio

indicators.note: what we hear is the sound of the word rather than its spelling

parts.note: tenners are ten-pound banknotes, and the word sounds like the singers

explanation.surface: A listener describes the musical notes coming from a celebrated vocal trio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks musical but means banknotes: a tenner is a British ten-pound note. The famous trio is the Three Tenors (Pavarotti, Domingo, Carreras).
explanation.definitionFit: The Three Tenors were a celebrated operatic trio, so its members are high male voices of that kind.

clue.text: Dispatch a pair of players north to get instrument

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means reading upwards, from the bottom of the grid to the top

parts.note: to dispatch someone is to kill them
taken as written
North and South are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: An orchestra manager sends two musicians up north to fetch an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named by compass point, and North-South is one partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare drum is a percussion instrument with wires stretched under its lower skin.

clue.text: At Christmas they traditionally help themselves? Not half!

indicators.note: not half tells us to drop one of the two halves of the word

parts.note: taken as written; a ten-letter word

explanation.surface: Do Santa's helpers at Christmas help themselves? Not half!
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the first five letters of the ten leaves the answer. 'Not half!' is also British slang for 'very much so'.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore Santa's elves build the toys at the North Pole, so they are his traditional Christmas helpers.

clue.text: A Christmas Carol quartet — good entertainers

parts.note: G is the usual abbreviation for good
hosts entertain guests

explanation.surface: A Christmas Carol is staged by four fine performers.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickens's A Christmas Carol has four spirits visiting Scrooge: Marley and the spirits of Christmas Past, Present and Yet to Come.
explanation.definitionFit: The four apparitions who visit Scrooge in Dickens's story are spirits of the dead and of Christmas.

clue.text: Three fliers from France sent to me after three others

definitions.text: Three fliers from France sent to me after three others

parts.note: surface reading: three French pilots or birds arriving

parts.words: sent to me after three others
parts.note: setter's reading: the third day's gift in The Twelve Days of Christmas, sent by my true love after a partridge and two turtle doves

explanation.walkthrough: The carol's third day brings 'three French hens'; the three earlier gifts are the partridge and the two turtle doves.
explanation.definitionFit: In the carol The Twelve Days of Christmas the true love sends three French poultry birds on the third day.

clue.text: It's not as ruined as places like Waterloo

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so its letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim that some battlefield is less devastated than Waterloo.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo suggests the battle, but it is the London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo is a major London rail terminus, an example of a railway stop.

clue.text: Cast start retiring
Floundering, showing weakness crossing line

indicators.note: one thing crossing another straddles it, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: a failing is a weakness, and failing is showing weakness
L is the usual abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone is floundering, visibly weak as they cross a finishing line.
explanation.definitionFit: Floundering means struggling clumsily, thrashing about, which is what flailing describes.

clue.text: Jovial deliveryman contributing to pleasant atmosphere

indicators.note: the answer contributes some of its letters to the words that follow, so it sits inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A cheerful postman helps keep the mood pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas is a jolly figure who delivers presents down chimneys, a whimsical courier.

clue.text: Very old, truly an improvised piece of organ music

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very

indicators.note: something improvised is made up on the spot, so these letters are thrown into a fresh order

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A really old organ piece was in truth improvised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an' is part of the anagram fodder, not a link word, despite reading like the article before 'improvised piece'.
explanation.definitionFit: A voluntary is a solo organ piece played before or after a church service, often improvised.

clue.text: and 14 Across and 29 Down: Bearers of gifts when tree is arranged, including me

parts.note: cross-reference padding: the answer continues in the two other linked lights

indicators.note: things arranged are put into an order, here a new order of the letters

parts.note: the letters taken as written
taken as written and added to the mix

explanation.surface: Gift-bearers arrive once the Christmas tree has been set up, and the speaker is among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including me' adds the two letters of 'me' to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi of the Nativity story brought gold, frankincense and myrrh to the infant Jesus.

clue.text: One of three I saw arriving this morning, going by air? Sea, actually

definitions.text: One of three I saw arriving this morning, going by air? Sea, actually

parts.words: One of three I saw arriving this morning, going by air?
parts.note: surface reading: three aircraft seen landing this morning
setter's reading: going by the air (tune) of the carol I Saw Three ___s, which come sailing in on Christmas Day in the morning

explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' means a tune: the carol I Saw Three Ships has vessels come sailing in on Christmas Day in the morning. The question mark flags the twist.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol's vessels travel by sea, so the answer is a seagoing craft rather than an aircraft.

clue.text: See 12
Third descriptor of Boxing Day snow is not odd

definitions.text: Third descriptor of Boxing Day snow
definitions.meaning: first meaning: Good King Wenceslas sees snow 'deep and crisp and ___' on the Feast of Stephen

explanation.walkthrough: The carol Good King Wenceslas is set on the Feast of Stephen, 26 December, which Britain calls Boxing Day; the snow lay 'deep and crisp and' this.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol's third adjective for the snow means smooth and level, and the word also means divisible by two.

clue.text: Open anger that may be smouldering in church

definitions.text: that may be smouldering in church

parts.note: frank means candid, open
to incense someone is to anger them

explanation.surface: Undisguised rage that may be simmering among a congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smouldering' suggests suppressed anger, but it literally means burning slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic resin is burnt in censers during church services, so it smoulders there.

clue.text: Farm animal introduced to new sort of tonic safe to consume

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: something introduced to another is put inside it
a sort of something is a variant of it, so the following letters appear in a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
an ox is a bovine farm animal

explanation.surface: A cow is given a new kind of tonic that is safe to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is not poisonous can be eaten or drunk safely.

clue.text: and 32 Across: Things to be unpacked today, such as three Across answers

definitions.text: Things to be unpacked today, such as three Across answers

parts.note: surface reading: perhaps luggage or shopping to sort out
setter's reading: the Magi's gifts appear as three across entries in this grid

explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared on Christmas Day; the three gifts of the Magi (16, 25 and 30 Across) are examples.
explanation.definitionFit: Gifts unwrapped on 25 December include the gold, frankincense and myrrh in the grid.

clue.text: Learner in oversized uniform

indicators.note: in places one element inside the other

parts.note: fat means large, oversized
L is for learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A trainee is lost in a uniform several sizes too big.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like the clothing, but it is the adjective meaning even.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat means level and unvarying, so uniform in the sense of the same throughout.

clue.text: Crazily firing without notice — that's demeaning

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the first part goes around the second
crazily means in a wild, disordered way, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters taken as written
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: Sacking staff on a whim and with no notice is beneath anyone's dignity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without notice' reads as 'with no warning', but 'without' here means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Infra dig, short for Latin infra dignitatem, means beneath one's dignity.

clue.text: Servant a long time retained by vessel's bosses

indicators.note: what is retained by something is held within it

parts.note: a liner is an ocean ship; with the 's the letter S follows
a man is a manservant
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A servant kept on for years by a shipping firm's owners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel's' gives the ship plus a final S: the pair of pieces goes inside between its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Line managers are the supervisors directly above an employee, their immediate superiors.

clue.text: Customer parking right in the middle of a lot

parts.note: P is the sign for parking

indicators.note: something in the middle of a phrase sits inside it

parts.note: a ton is a lot
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A shopper leaves a car right in the middle of a car park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' suggests a parking lot, but it means a large amount: a ton.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron is a regular customer of a shop, restaurant or business.

clue.text: In game on board, mostly moves cautiously

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
chess is a game played on a board

explanation.surface: Playing a board game, someone mostly makes careful moves.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch forward is to move very slowly and carefully, a little at a time.

clue.text: Rookie in trio having change of heart

indicators.note: a change of heart alters the middle, so the central letters swap places

parts.note: taken as written; its two middle letters are swapped

explanation.surface: A newcomer in a musical trio has a change of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of heart' usually means a change of mind; here it means altering the word's central letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiro (or tyro) is a beginner or novice, the same as a rookie.

clue.text: What athletes aim for — and archers

definitions.meaning: second meaning: what archers aim for, the bullseye of a target

explanation.walkthrough: 'and archers' borrows the start of the clue: what archers aim for too. The centre of an archery target is coloured this.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletes target first place and its medal, and archers aim at the bullseye, both called by this precious metal's name.

clue.text: Philanthropist's name inscribed in entrance

indicators.note: something inscribed in a surface is written within it

parts.note: a door is an entrance
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A benefactor's name is carved over the doorway of the building they funded.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor gives money to good causes, as a philanthropist does.

clue.text: Resort around spring in part of Europe

parts.note: a spa is a resort built around a mineral spring
taken as written

explanation.surface: A holiday resort somewhere in Europe, visited in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests the season, but it is a water source, and the whole phrase describes one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is a country occupying most of the Iberian peninsula in south-west Europe.

clue.text: Short publication I provided for some on Christmas journey with travel guide

definitions.text: some on Christmas journey with travel guide

parts.note: mag is short for magazine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A slim travel magazine is handed out to people on a festive trip with a tour guide.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'travel guide' is the star of Bethlehem, which the wise men followed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi journeyed to Bethlehem following a star, so they were travellers led by a guide in the sky.

clue.text: Peacemaking activity I dominate improperly

indicators.note: improperly means wrongly, so the letters are set out in the wrong order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A would-be peacemaker confesses to taking over the talks.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediation is intervention by a third party to settle a dispute, an act of peacemaking.

clue.text: See 12
Run repeatedly into my hospital for medicinal gum

indicators.note: into means placed inside what follows

parts.note: taken as written
H is the map sign for hospital
R is the cricket abbreviation for run, given twice

explanation.surface: Someone keeps running into the hospital to fetch a medicinal gum.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrrh is an aromatic gum resin used in medicine and perfume, one of the Magi's gifts.

clue.text: Small quantity of liquor, or two other drinks

parts.note: the first drink: nog, a strong ale or eggnog
the second drink: the spirit gin

explanation.surface: A tot of spirits, or a couple of other drinks instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Nog is the drink in eggnog, an old word for strong ale.
explanation.definitionFit: A noggin is a small measure of spirits, about a quarter of a pint.

clue.text: See 18
